implementationTasks.title: I1. Persist versioned task intents and replay receipts
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/task-server-bus/index.html and workbench.json (AGT-2905, companion to AGT-W49 and AGT-W57), the current recorded decision for this slice, AGENTS.md and the relevant domain maps before implementation. The Dossier baseline is develop 50b767f014386fc0b4c00d1bb9db8c554be72d0f; recheck current code instead of copying stale line numbers. Keep task authority and Git/worktree mutation in the platform. Use docs/system/domains/model-routing-policy.md for any model selection; quota must not cross correctness floors. This card covers only its bounded acceptanceScope. Update affected public contracts, report changed files and exact verification; do not commit or push from the run agent.

Implement D6: one server-owned accepted command for start/continue, optional CLI/model/thinking overrides, prompt text and requested lane action. Current TaskRunnerService.ContinueJobAsync calls TaskMutationService setters, RecordUserFollowUpAsync and QueueFollowUp in separate writes. Add a command ID, task intent revision and payload digest with expected-revision conflict handling. Persist the canonical command/receipt before projecting prompt history, pending-intent.json and Ready position, and reconcile incomplete projections on restart. Existing /api/tasks/{id}/continue clients must keep their mode guard and queued/started response semantics. Same key plus changed payload must conflict. Distinguish task intent revision from RunAttempt fence/authority epoch. Provide the admitted intent API/read model needed by I10 without migrating local execution in this slice. No new external broker.

Dependencies: none; I10 and I7 consume these receipts. Test replay, concurrent different prompts, mode rejection before writes, crash after each persisted boundary and restart projection repair with deterministic storage/fault injection.

Acceptance:
- An accepted command survives restart and produces one continuation note, one pending intent and one intended promotion.
- Same command replay is idempotent; changed payload or stale expected revision conflicts without partial mutation.
- Claim freezes the accepted execution inputs; subsequent task edits cannot change the active attempt.
- Existing remote continuation and concept/planning mode guards remain covered by regression tests.

Implement D7 in RemoteRunStopRequestStore, TaskRunnerEndpoints stop, LeaseEndpoints renewal, TaskServerClient and LeaseHeartbeat. Replace the task-key-only in-memory pending stop with a durable directive ID bound to task, AttemptId, Fence, AuthorityEpoch, issuer, reason, creation/expiry and acknowledgement. Deliver only to the exact current target; do not rebind a directive to the next round. Keep the worker authoritative long enough to report Stopped and preserve salvage. - An old stop never cancels a successor attempt, including the same task and host.

Implement the report/evidence half of D8. In production V1ReviewPlaneEndpoints the authority summary can settle before full ReviewReportRequest is projected; RemoteReviewEvidenceProjectionQueue is an in-memory Channel and Duplicate returns without enqueueing. Introduce durable report storage keyed by attempt, fence, epoch, idempotency key and canonical full payload digest, with an evidence-projection receipt and resumable work record. ACK only after the full handoff is durable. Restart must recover pending projection even if the runner already accepted the ACK and cleaned up. Compare standalone TaskServerReviewStore.ReportReviewAsync, which already persists report_json and report_sha256 transactionally. Preserve exact subject checks, citations, placement and bounded projection retries; include typed terminal projection failure. Do not rerun review to rebuild lost projections.

Dependencies: none; I4 consumes the durable report. Fault-inject settlement-before-enqueue, ACK-before-projection, restart mid-projection, duplicate identical report and same key with altered artifacts/verdicts but unchanged summary.

Acceptance:
- Full accepted report bytes or content-addressed references survive restart before ACK.
- Idempotency binds all semantic report content; altered verdicts/artifacts cannot masquerade as Duplicate.
- Projection resumes from durable work without re-review and is idempotent at every output boundary.
- Terminal projection failure exposes attempt/report identity and a repairable receipt.

Implement the integration/lane half of D8. RemoteDeliverySettlementStore currently stores a best-effort sidecar with IntegrationPending, IntegrationSettled and LaneSettled, and RemoteDeliveryIntegrationCoordinator coalesces only in process. Make stage ownership durable and generation-checked using the current ReviewAttempt and report identity, with compare-and-swap advancement or the selected equivalent single-owner transaction. Move first-report integration waiting out of the HTTP acknowledgement path after its durable work receipt exists. Preserve RemoteDeliveryIntegrationPolicy gate admission, MergeIntoDevelopRunner platform ownership, remote-push/containment proof, ordering per integration branch and AutoReviewDeliveryResumeService behavior. A successful review is not integration proof; an integrated commit is not a completed lane receipt. Preserve interrupted integration journal recovery and agent-round outcomes.

Dependencies: I3 full report receipt. Crash tests: accepted report before gate work, before/after merge and push, after integration before lane, concurrent endpoint/sweep, obsolete review generation. Prove no repeat merge and no repeat review, plus rejection/parking behavior.

Acceptance:
- Report ACK does not wait for integration after durable handoff is committed.
- Only the current review generation advances stages; concurrent resume passes cannot regress or steal ownership.
- Restart reaches the correct integration and lane outcome using durable evidence without repeating a passed review.
- Integrated remains contingent on remote containment/push proof; failed gates produce typed failure and correct lane.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:

Implement D9 after reproducing the measured gap. docs/task-server-bus/assets/tunnel-outage-2026-09-24-25.log records AGT-2887 stop-before 2026-09-25T08:17:09.6166384Z and lease-loss at 08:18:10Z; AGT-2889 receives Expired, both quarantine and later claim higher fences. In LeaseHeartbeat.RunAsync the network request can outlive the deadline before the catch checks it. Reproduce with fake time and a never-completing renewal, then enforce a cancellation/reaping deadline independently of HTTP completion and bound each request by remaining issued authority. Preserve DurableLeaseAuthority, durable slot/outbox journals, RemoteTaskRunner quarantine and CodingFinalizationReconciler replay. Define compatibility-versus-standalone process-unknown reconciliation explicitly; no new claim without the required no-overlap proof. A local fence prevents writes, not zombie process execution.

Dependencies: none. Read orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html before changing outcome/recovery logic and maintain its incident log. Test transport loss, late successful renewal, wall-clock movement, duplicate/old completion, server restart, pending valid finalization and unknown process generation. A live controlled outage drill must be authorized and use disposable tasks; do not interrupt production for verification.

Acceptance:
- Fake-time regression proves worker cancellation is initiated at the bounded local authority deadline despite hung I/O.
- Process generation is reconciled before replacement; late renewal cannot restore rejected authority.
- Expired work is quarantined with attempt/fence/SHA and cannot become an accepted delivery by replay.
- Valid accepted-delivery replays remain idempotent, and a controlled recovery drill records timestamps and identities.

Implement D10/D11: many eligible hosts per class, with the operator workstation as the same runner-host family. Start from LeaseEndpoints project assignment filtering, V1ReviewExecutorRegistry, TaskServer capability/registration store, RunnerOptions and both daemon admission loops. Add a project execution requirement/pool selector that resolves authenticated current registrations by role, repository access, toolchain/provider health and fresh capacity; retain optional explicit host pins as narrowing policy. Do not grant execution from self-advertised trust alone. Maintain separate coding/review service identities, credentials, roots and live slot budgets on a shared physical host. Document baseline profiles: Linux 2+ hosts at 2 coding/2 review slots each; Windows 0–N at 1/1 when required; workstation 0–N at 1/0, all configurable and load gated. Adding a host changes eligible supply, not task ownership; draining/removal stops claims and preserves current leases until settled or reconciled.

Dependencies: none; share role requirements with I9. Test two same-class hosts competing for one task, capability expiry/re-registration, lowered slots, host drain/removal, new host join, workstation-only repository constraint, and project default sequential execution. No new Workstation Agent process or Quality Host Agent role.

Acceptance:
- Two hosts can satisfy one project requirement set without rewriting a singleton runner assignment.
- Claims enforce principal permissions, fresh capabilities, host role slots/load and project maxParallelism.
- Host join/drain/removal cannot overlap authority or orphan a silently owned task.
- Workstation uses the same host contract with explicit capabilities and preserves browser-edge security boundaries.

implementationTasks.title: I10. Drive local and remote execution through the engine bus adapter
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:

Implement the execution-adapter half of D5 using I1 admitted intent/receipts. The standalone OrchestratorEngineService already claims orchestration stages via EngineTaskServerClient, but its handlers inspect payloads; PostProcessingLoop is a marker and GateDispatchLoop reads prior statuses. Production TaskRunnerService local start/continue still calls ProjectRunner directly while remote follow-ups queue. Introduce an engine-side task-fact/intent adapter that reads the admitted input/revision, proposes lane/model/prompt/continue/hold/park/review actions and receives Task Server validation/receipts. Route local start/continue through the same admitted work claim semantics as an ordinary runner host; keep the existing local executor adapter if needed during migration, but no engine-to-daemon start/stop RPC. Do not copy authority state into the engine or turn it into another workflow engine. Maintain current prep/review policy and bounded project concurrency. Extend stage lease renewal if any migrated handler can exceed its current lease.

Dependencies: I1; consume I9 quality plans and I4 settlement state when their slices land. Test engine restart/replay, expired engine lease, stale task revision, local-versus-remote intent equivalence, and no direct daemon network dependency. Keep coding agents free of platform Git/worker lifecycle ownership. Update the orchestrator domain/contract for the final adapter boundary.

Acceptance:
- Engine actions enter through Task Server admission and durable receipts; no direct execution control reaches a daemon.
- Local and remote start/continue obey the same accepted-intent, claim and fencing semantics.
- Engine replay and lease expiry cannot apply a decision twice or against changed task state.
- Existing policy, project sequential default and shared quality/integration boundaries remain intact.
